title: History Has No Chill
blurb: Presidents, scientists, emperors and composers, with true stories too weird to make up.

cards.say: John Adams [was the first president to live in the White House], [lived in the White House for all four years of his presidency], [left town before the man who beat him was sworn in], and [died on the very same day as Thomas Jefferson].
cards.real: Adams moved into the newly built White House on November 1, 1800, with only about four months left in his term.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House (on November 1, 1800, Adams became the first president to take residence in the building)
https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/november-1/john-adams-moves-into-white-house (moved in November 1, 1800; Jefferson sworn in March 4, 1801)
https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/november-1/john-adams-moves-into-white-house (as Jefferson was sworn in on March 4, 1801, Adams was already on his way back to Massachusetts)
https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/thomas-jefferson-and-john-adams-die (both died July 4, 1826)

cards.say: James Madison [stood just 5 feet 4 inches tall], [once suggested hiring Portugal's navy to fight pirates], [has his face on the 5,000 dollar bill], and [lost a 1789 race for Congress to James Monroe].
cards.real: Madison beat James Monroe for a seat in the first House of Representatives in 1789. Monroe later followed him as president.
src: https://www.mentalfloss.com/history/presidents/16-fun-facts-james-madisons-birthday (at 5 feet 4 inches, the shortest president)
https://founders.archives.gov/documents/Madison/01-15-02-0144 (House debate, February 1794: he would hire the Portuguese ships of war against the Algerine corsairs instead of building a fleet)
https://www.mentalfloss.com/history/presidents/16-fun-facts-james-madisons-birthday (Madison's face appeared on the 5,000 dollar bill)
https://www.mentalfloss.com/history/presidents/16-fun-facts-james-madisons-birthday (he defeated Monroe for a House seat in 1789)

cards.say: Ulysses S. Grant [graduated first in his class at West Point], [was born with the first name Hiram], [was arrested for speeding in his horse carriage while president], and [signed the law that made Yellowstone the first national park].
cards.real: Grant finished 21st out of 39 cadets in West Point's class of 1843, right in the middle of the pack.
src: https://www.nps.gov/articles/000/grant-s-early-years.htm (graduated 21st of 39 in 1843)
https://www.nps.gov/people/ulysses-s-grant.htm (born Hiram Ulysses Grant)

https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/when-president-ulysses-s-grant-was-arrested-for-speeding-in-a-horse-drawn-carriage-180981916/ (arrested by officer William West in 1872; the arrest is not in dispute)
https://www.nps.gov/people/ulysses-s-grant.htm (signed the Yellowstone act on March 1, 1872)

cards.say: Franklin D. Roosevelt [moved Thanksgiving up a week in 1939 to help stores], [was the first sitting president to appear on TV], [was the first sitting president to speak on the radio], and [had a dog who got his own statue at the FDR Memorial].
cards.real: Presidents were on the radio years before FDR: Warren Harding in 1922 and Calvin Coolidge in 1923. FDR made radio famous with his fireside chats.
src: https://www.stripes.com/history/2021-11-24/franklin-roosevelt-moved-thanksgiving-week-1939-3742553.html (moved from Nov. 30 to Nov. 23, 1939, at merchants' request, for more Christmas shopping days)
https://its.ntia.gov/this-month-in-its-history/april-1939/ (April 30, 1939: the first appearance on television by a sitting president)

https://hardingpresidentialsites.org/2022/05/29/first-presidential-radio-broadcast-marks-100-year-anniversary/ (Harding spoke over radio in 1922) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge (December 6, 1923 address broadcast)
https://www.nps.gov/articles/fala.htm (Fala's statue sits beside FDR's at the memorial; the only presidential pet so honored)

cards.say: Calvin Coolidge [was born on the Fourth of July], [adopted a raccoon that was sent to be his Thanksgiving dinner], [was sworn in as president by his own father, by lamplight], and [served as governor of Vermont before he became president].
cards.real: Coolidge was born in Vermont but made his career in Massachusetts, where he was governor from 1919 to 1921.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge (born July 4, 1872)

https://www.whitehousehistory.org/questions/what-are-some-unusual-animals-that-have-lived-in-and-around-the-white-house (Rebecca, sent from Mississippi in 1926 to be served for Thanksgiving dinner, adopted as a pet)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge (his father, a notary public, gave the oath by the light of a kerosene lamp on August 3, 1923)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge (48th governor of Massachusetts, 1919 to 1921)

cards.say: Isaac Newton [was born on the very day that Galileo died], [hunted down counterfeiters while working at England's Royal Mint], [was knighted by Queen Anne in 1705], and [served two short terms in Parliament].
cards.real: Galileo died on January 8, 1642. Newton was born almost a year later, on Christmas Day 1642 by England's old calendar.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (born 25 December 1642 Old Style) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galileo_Galilei (died 8 January 1642)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (Warden then Master of the Royal Mint; prosecuted 28 coiners)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (knighted by Queen Anne, April 1705)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Newton (MP for Cambridge University 1689 to 1690 and 1701 to 1702)

cards.say: Albert Einstein [turned down an offer to be president of Israel], [hated socks so much that he refused to wear them], [won his Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity], and [was such a bad sailor that his neighbors had to rescue him].
cards.real: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics was for explaining the photoelectric effect, work very different from relativity.
src: https://www.livescience.com/physics-mathematics/32-fun-and-random-facts-about-albert-einstein (offered in 1952, declined)
https://www.livescience.com/physics-mathematics/32-fun-and-random-facts-about-albert-einstein (disliked socks so much he refused to wear them, since they develop holes)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Einstein (1921 prize for services to theoretical physics, especially the law of the photoelectric effect)
https://www.livescience.com/physics-mathematics/32-fun-and-random-facts-about-albert-einstein (neighbors often had to rescue him when his boat capsized)

cards.say: Napoleon [wrote a romance novella years before he became emperor], [had his soldiers shoot the nose off Egypt's Great Sphinx], [was born a year after Genoa handed his home island, Corsica, to France], and [died before anyone took a photo that still survives today].
cards.real: Drawings from 1737 already show the Sphinx without its nose, decades before Napoleon was born. His army reached Egypt in 1798.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon (wrote the romantic novella Clisson et Eugenie in 1795; emperor from 18 May 1804)
https://www.smithsonianjourneys.org/blogs/blog/2022/09/15/photo-what-happened-to-the-sphinxs-nose (the cannonball story is a legend; Norden's 1737 drawings show no nose)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon (born in 1769, one year after the Republic of Genoa ceded Corsica to France by the 1768 Treaty of Versailles)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/View_from_the_Window_at_Le_Gras (oldest surviving photograph, 1827) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon (died 5 May 1821)

cards.say: The French Revolution [freed more than 100 prisoners when crowds stormed the Bastille], [briefly used official clocks with 10 hours in a day], [gave the world the metric system], and [began the same year George Washington became president].
cards.real: When crowds stormed the Bastille on July 14, 1789, the old fortress prison held just seven prisoners.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storming_of_the_Bastille (the prison contained only seven inmates on 14 July 1789)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_time (1793 decree: ten hours a day; mandatory use suspended 7 April 1795)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metric_system (first devised in the early days of the French Revolution; launched in France in 1799)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington (inaugurated April 30, 1789) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storming_of_the_Bastille (July 14, 1789)

cards.say: Ludwig van Beethoven [has no known birthday, only the date he was baptized], [scratched Napoleon's name off a symphony he had named after him], [had to be turned around to see the crowd cheering his Ninth Symphony], and [moved to Vienna in 1792 to take lessons from Mozart].
cards.real: Mozart had died in December 1791. When Beethoven moved to Vienna in 1792, he studied with Joseph Haydn instead.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (baptized 17 December 1770; exact birth date undocumented)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (Eroica, first titled Bonaparte; name scratched off in 1804)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (7 May 1824 premiere; Caroline Unger turned him around to see the applause)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven (moved to Vienna November 1792 and studied with Haydn) + https://www.themorgan.org/exhibitions/online/mozart/418 (Mozart 1756-1791)

cards.say: Peter the Great [became tsar at age 10, sharing the throne with his half-brother], [worked four months in a Dutch shipyard under a fake name], [moved Russia's New Year's Day from January 1 to September 1], and [personally shaved the beards off his own party guests].
cards.real: It was the other way around: in 1699, Peter moved Russia's New Year from September 1 to January 1.
src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_the_Great (chosen tsar at 10; ruled jointly with his elder half-brother Ivan V until 1696)

https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/why-tsar-peter-great-established-beard-tax-180964693/ (traveled as Sergeant Pyotr Mikhaylov; four months at a Dutch East India Company shipyard) + https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_the_Great
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_the_Great (in 1699 moved the start of the year from 1 September to 1 January)
https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/why-tsar-peter-great-established-beard-tax-180964693/ (personally shaved the beards from his horrified guests at a reception)

cards.say: Ada Lovelace [grew up without ever knowing her father, the poet Lord Byron], [saw her program run on Charles Babbage's finished Analytical Engine], [wrote what historians call the first computer program, in 1843], and [predicted that computing machines could one day make music].
cards.real: Babbage's Analytical Engine was never finished. Only a small piece of it was ever built, so her program never ran in her lifetime.
src: https://www.britannica.com/story/ada-lovelace-the-first-computer-programmer (Ada never met her father; the marriage lasted little more than a year)
https://www.britannica.com/story/ada-lovelace-the-first-computer-programmer (only a small piece of the Analytical Engine was ever built)
https://www.britannica.com/story/ada-lovelace-the-first-computer-programmer (regarded by computer historians as the first computer program)
https://www.britannica.com/story/ada-lovelace-the-first-computer-programmer (the engine could work on things besides number, such as musical notes)
